topic: Law change: FSSAI makes a standard milk logo (white milk drop on a blue square) compulsory on the principal display panel of all milk and milk products, including composite milk products, from 1 July 2028; minimum logo size 6 mm to 16 mm by panel area (Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Second Amendment Regulations, 2026, amending Schedule I of the 2020 Regulations under Section 92, FSS Act, 2006; notified November 2026)

slides.title: A **milk logo** on every dairy pack
slides.subtitle: FSSAI has made one standard logo compulsory on all milk and milk products. The rule starts on **1 July 2028**.
slides.cite: **Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Second Amendment Regulations, 2026** · FSSAI · notified November 2026

slides.label: What is new
slides.title: One **standard logo** for dairy
bullets: FSSAI has changed **Schedule I** of its Labelling and Display Regulations, 2020, using its power under **Section 92** of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
The logo is a **white milk drop** inside a **blue square**.
It must be printed on the **principal display panel**, which is the main front face of the pack.

slides.label: Which products
slides.title: Milk, curd, paneer and **more**
bullets: It covers **all milk and milk products**, including **composite milk products**, as listed in FSSAI's 2011 product standards.
FSSAI says the aim is to make it simpler for shoppers to **readily identify** products in this category.
The logo has a minimum size. It ranges from **6 mm** on the smallest packs to **16 mm** on the largest, based on the front panel area.

slides.label: When it applies
slides.title: Not yet: from **1 July 2028**
bullets: The rule comes into force on **1 July 2028**. Until then, a pack without this logo does not break this new rule.
The long gap gives dairy companies time to redesign their **packaging and labels**.
From that date, every milk and milk product pack must carry it.

slides.label: Keep in mind
slides.title: What this rule does **not** do
bullets: FSSAI's separate idea (September 2026) that non-milk products should not be sold as **"paneer"** is only a **proposal** so far. It is not part of this rule.
Keep reading the **ingredients** and **use-by date** on every pack, logo or no logo.
This post is for information only, not legal advice.

caption:
Soon, your milk packet will carry a new logo 🥛✅

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has notified the Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Second Amendment Regulations, 2026. Under this change, all milk and milk products, including composite milk products, must carry one standard logo: a white milk drop inside a blue square, printed on the main front panel of the pack.

FSSAI says the aim is to make it simpler for consumers to readily identify products in this category. The logo has a minimum size based on the front panel area, from 6 mm on the smallest packs to 16 mm on the largest. The rule comes into force on 1 July 2028, so companies have time to change their packaging. Until then, a pack without the logo does not break this new rule.

Keep in mind: FSSAI's separate idea that non-milk products should not be sold as "paneer" is still only a proposal and is not part of this rule. Whatever the logo, keep checking the ingredients and use-by date on every pack.

Law: Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Second Amendment Regulations, 2026, amending Schedule I of the 2020 Regulations (Section 92, Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006)
Issued by: FSSAI, notified November 2026, in force from 1 July 2028

This post is for information only, not legal advice.
